LESSON: STRETCHING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.4: Stretching
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Stretching, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is stretching important during a physical activity?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the body parts involved in stretching,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Stretching in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. perform stretching in different directions for flexibility,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Stretching in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. enjoy stretching in different directions for body fitness. ● Learners to talk/write/type/point the body parts involved in stretching. ● Learners to demonstrate stretching in different directions with peers. ● Learners to practise stretching in different directions. Safety precautions for all the learners should be observed with extra caution taken for learners with health conditions. ● Learners to practise stretching in different positions. ● Learners to collaboratively, play appropriate games involving stretching while observing safety. Learners with postural Why is stretching important during a physical activity? 11 defects could use alternative functional parts of the body, perform an alternative corresponding activity, or perform at their level of functional ability. ● Learners to sing action songs on body parts involved in stretching. Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech, hum, mime or use alternative mode of communications. ● Learners to team up to use digital devices to record performances on stretching for future reference. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, assistive technology or be supported.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Stretching in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Stretching together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration as the learner actively talks about parts of the body that are used in stretching.

● Creativity and Imagination as the learner creatively stretches in directions and in positions.

● Digital literacy as the learner uses digital devices to record performances on stretching.

12

Values:
● Responsibility is promoted as the learner observes safety of self and others during stretching activities.

● Love is nurtured as the learner appreciates the ability of others stretching in different positions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and security is promoted as the learner stretches to a reasonable limit to avoid injuries while in different positions.

Link to other learning areas:

Environmental Activities is nurtured as the learner stretches to different directions of the compass point.

Suggested learning resources:

Open space, field makers, landing mats, flash cards, digital devices, musical instruments, pictures, audio /visual recordings of

music and stretching skills, relevant virtual sites, relevant attire, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm

braces, adapted digital devices with filter keys/key guards/larger mouse/head control input devices such as head wand
